scope: two independently authenticated stdio MCP bridges connected to one local daemon over loopback
steps: The user-control CLI issued two private tickets and generated separate bridge configurations.
Two bridge processes redeemed separate tickets and exposed the same registered MCP tool set.
The main bridge created, readied and published a task; the worker bridge claimed the task.
Main selected shared workspace; worker declared and acquired an exclusive path lease.
Both sessions submitted different cognition claims for workspace.driver and the runtime recorded a discrepancy.
Main proposed a contract and both participant bridges accepted their slots.
Worker sent a message; main claimed, presented and acknowledged it.
Worker prepared/preflighted/started the workspace, wrote a real file, recorded the result and submitted it.
Main accepted the submitted result and the task reached completed.
A worker attempt to claim the already completed task was rejected, preserving ownership boundaries.
limits: The host processes were launched by the smoke runner, not by a real Codex/OpenCode/DeepSeek UI.
User decision resolution, project completion confirmation and daemon restart are covered by the Python M1 integration and remain separate gates for the final product.
Temporary IDs, ticket material and absolute paths are intentionally omitted.
